components.html:
Focus

Today’s tasks

narrative.overview: LifeOS is a dark-first personal operating system: information-dense enough to operate daily, calm enough to remain open for long sessions, and recognizable through its per-module Aurora headers. Its visual identity comes from cool ink surfaces, restrained borders, Montserrat typography, truthful data states, and precise module accents—not generic glass, heavy shadows, or decorative cards. The approved mock defines visual intent. Mock and API implementations reuse the same presentation components wherever practical. Data-source differences belong at the adapter or view-model layer and must never create alternate visual systems.
keyCharacteristics: Aurora imagery carries module identity; content surfaces stay restrained.
Compact, aligned, numeric dashboards with honest empty semantics.
Calm, fast interaction feedback without page-wide decorative motion.

rules.name: Module Identity
rules.body: Finance is emerald; Habits and Goals are distinct teals; Gym is cyan; Reading is violet; Study is blue; Analytics is cyan/blue; Settings is slate; Profile uses its selected personal accent. Never replace these identities with one universal product accent.

rules.name: Accent Restraint
rules.body: Module color belongs on icons, meaningful series, selection, focus, and small indicators. Large competing color fields are avoided.

rules.name: Stable Panel
rules.body: A panel does not animate merely because it mounted or refreshed.

dos: Preserve the pinned v0 visual foundation within Today while keeping global Aurora definitions authoritative elsewhere.
Retain mobile DOM/focus order and active-theme selection contrast when adjusting Today.
Treat the approved mock as the source of visual intent.
Share presentation components between mock and API modes.
Preserve module accents and Aurora identities across themes.
Use real controls with visible focus and reduced-motion support.
Distinguish passive, interactive, selected, and elevated surfaces semantically.
donts: Propagate Today tokens, fonts, corners or atmosphere into unmigrated routes.
Replace live application capabilities or data contracts with v0 fixtures or local demo state.
Redesign LifeOS into a generic SaaS dashboard.
Create alternate mock and API visual systems.
Animate every panel or add bouncy decorative movement.
Use large competing module-colored surfaces in Analytics.
Nest bordered cards when a section row or separator is sufficient.
Replace custom LifeOS controls with browser-native substitutes.
